newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government considers end to emergency rule.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government considers end to emergency rule.

text.p: Turkey's government is looking to abolish emergency rule, enforced in the mainly Kurdish southeast to counter a rebel insurgency, a cabinet spokesman said on Wednesday.

"The lifting of emergency rule at the end of the year at the latest and if possible earlier, in October or November, was discussed," spokesman Ahat Andican said at a briefing on Tuesday evening's cabinet meeting.

Emergency rule, one step short of martial law, has been in force in nine southeastern provinces since 1987. The rule gives police and security forces wide powers of arrest and detention in their fight against Kurdish guerrillas in the region.
Andican said there were plans to set up a coordination council to help overcome the region's problems after the lifting of emergency rule.
The coordination council would look into the question of repopulating villages emptied by migration to urban areas as a result of the Kurdish conflict, he said.
The previous Islamist-led government, replaced at the end of June by a secularist coalition, vowed to lift emergency rule but did not act on the pledge.
The proposed measure would effectively need approval from the military-dominated National Security Council.

More than 26,000 people have been killed in 13 years of conflict between the Turkish armed forces and the rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) who are fighting for independence or autonomy in the southeast.
